newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-MFI profits raise hopes for bumper Jan.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-MFI profits raise hopes for bumper Jan.

text.p: MFI Furniture Group Plc on Monday produced a 63 percent jump in profits and said this boded well for its key January sale even though Britain's housing market was still sluggish.
Britain's leading manufacturer and retailer of fitted kitchens and bedrooms said improved consumer confidence had helped profits and that the benefits of a housing upturn were still to come.
Pretax profits rose to 32.7 million pounds ($54.3 million) from 20.1 million on sales up 15.7 percent to 440.5 million from 380.6 million. The dividend rose by 13 percent to 1.7 pence.

"We're looking at January with a high degree of confidence," chairman Derek Hunt told a news conference. The group's traditional January sale, which starts on December 26, accounts for 30 percent of annual turnover.
The group, whose fortunes have been closely tied to the housing market, saw no sign yet of a revival.

Chief executive John Randall said, "We think the housing market is still dormant." He said the upturn in sales and profits had come from increased consumer confidence and the more buoyant economy. He said the housing market outside the south east of the country had not really changed.

Retail analysts said the group had probably benefited from the more robust consumer climate, but market share gains and its strong sales and profit performance also showed the success of its new MFI Homeworks format.
MFI's shares were broadly unchanged at 192.5 pence.

"People were reasonably pleased with the first half," said Nick Bubb, retail analyst at Mees Pierson. But there was caution on the shares because of worries over possible interest rate rises, he said.
Analysts said full year profit forecasts were being maintained at around 85 million to 90 million pounds.
MFI spent 37 million pounds during the first half, including 15 million on transforming its MFI stores into new-style MFI Homeworks, which carry a wider range of goods.
Hunt said these new format stores were producing a double figure sales uplift. The group has converted 78 of its 184 UK stores and expects it will take two more years to convert the entire chain.
Its new Howden Joinery business, which is not yet in profit, has 24 depots and there are plans to double the number in the next year. Hunt said MFI saw the potential for about 200 outlets eventually.

The group's 98 stores in France, which trade under the Hygena brand name, saw sales up 11 percent on a comparable store basis. But the group is cautious about immediate prospects for the business because of difficult trading conditions.
MFI has also opened three trial stores in Spain, two in Barcelona and one in Palma, Majorca, and would like five more in the Valencia and Malaga area.

The group is continuing its strategy of leasing its warehouse space to other retailers, which acts as a hedge against rent increases. Hunt said the group was concerned that out-of-town rents were poised to rise sharply.
